<div class="learn-box">
**What you will learn**

Measure time since entry, distinguish people from visits, and count visits by month and setting.
</div>

**You need:** the client packages and the Opal login from
[Getting started](book-00-start.html). This chapter uses `omop.questionnaire`.




``` r
library(dsOMOPClient)
conns <- ds.omop.login("https://localhost:8443", user = "administrator",
  password = "password", resource = "omop.questionnaire", server = "site")$conns
```



## Measure time from each person's first visit

An *index* is the event that starts a study episode. Index on each person's first
visit, then express first and last visit as days since that visit. People without
a visit cannot enter this indexed study.


``` r
visit <- omop_event("visit_occurrence")
visit_study <- omop_study(visit, outputs = "baseline", baseline = list(
  first_days = omop_first_date("visit_occurrence"),
  last_days = omop_last_date("visit_occurrence")))
recipe_execute(visit_study, out = c(baseline = "D_visit_study"), conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_visit_study$last_days", datasources = conns)
```

```
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "integer"
#>
#> $site$length
#> [1] 36
#>
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>   5%  10%  25%  50%  75%  90%  95% Mean
#>    0    0    0  366 1203 1203 1203  523
```

``` r
dsBaseClient::ds.numNA("D_visit_study$last_days", datasources = conns)
```

```
#> $site
#> [1] 0
```

The 36 valid values describe visitors. The last visit is 0, 366 or 1,203 days after
entry; zero includes people with only one visit. This is elapsed time between
recorded visits, not duration of observation. The first-visit offset is zero by definition.

An offset from a public fixed date, such as 2020-01-01, can be converted back to
an exact calendar date. Even a quantile may reveal a shared date when values are
tied. Use index-relative time for elapsed-time questions and month categories for
calendar summaries.

## Keep calendar dates private and summarise months

`omop_date("first_visit")` assigns an exact Date on the server; it does not let you
fetch dates. For a calendar summary, explicitly choose month precision.


``` r
months <- omop_recipe(variables = list(visit_month = omop_date("first_visit",
  omop_date_spec(precision = "month", level_range = c("2020-03-01", "2020-07-31")))),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
recipe_execute(months, out = c(people = "D_months"), conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_months$visit_month",
  useNA = "always", datasources = conns)$output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
```

```
#> D_months$visit_month
#> 2020-03 2020-06 2020-07      NA
#>      12      12      12      12
```

March, June and July each contain 12 first visitors.
Another 12 people have no visit. The public range declares the months to include;
it is not estimated by requesting the earliest and latest patient dates.

## Identify the setting

Chapter 4 found **9201, Inpatient Visit**, and **9202, Outpatient Visit**.
Check their names before selecting them:


``` r
settings <- ds.omop.concept.lookup(c(9201L, 9202L), conns = conns)$pooled
settings[c("concept_id", "concept_name", "domain_id")]
```



| concept_id|concept_name     |domain_id |
|----------:|:----------------|:---------|
|       9201|Inpatient Visit  |Visit     |
|       9202|Outpatient Visit |Visit     |

Both are Visit concepts. They select `visit_concept_id`, the care setting.
`visit_type_concept_id` instead describes how a record was obtained; filtering
that column for 9201 would not define inpatient care.

## Count visit rows by month and setting

A long table keeps one row per visit. Its `start_date` comes from
`visit_start_date`, and `concept_id` contains the labelled setting. Apply month
precision to the event dates before asking for a two-way table.


``` r
long_visits <- omop_recipe(
  events = list(visits = omop_event("visit_occurrence", concepts = c(9201L, 9202L), name = "visits")),
  outputs = omop_output("visits", format = "long", sources = "visits"),
  date_spec = omop_date_spec(precision = "month"))
recipe_execute(long_visits, out = c(visits = "D_visits"), conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_visits$start_date",
  "D_visits$concept_id", useNA = "no",
  datasources = conns)$output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
```



|        | Inpatient Visit| Outpatient Visit|
|:-------|---------------:|----------------:|
|2020-03 |               0|               12|
|2020-06 |               0|               12|
|2020-07 |               0|               12|
|2021-03 |              12|                0|
|2023-10 |              12|                0|

The table counts 24 inpatient and 36 outpatient visits: 60 records from 36
visitors. The outpatient visits are in March, June and July 2020; inpatient
visits are in March 2021 and October 2023, with 12 in each month. These are visit counts, so a person may contribute twice.

## Exercises

**1. Count visits per person.** Include people who never visited. Explain how the
counts relate to the 60 rows in the long table.

<details><summary>Solution 1</summary>


``` r
counts <- omop_recipe(variables = list(visits = omop_variable(event = visit,
  reducer = omop_reduce("count"))))
recipe_execute(counts, out = "D_visit_counts", conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_visit_counts$visits",
  datasources = conns)$output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
```

```
#> D_visit_counts$visits
#>  0  1  2 NA
#> 12 12 24  0
```

Twelve people have zero visits, 12 have one and 24 have two.
Thus 12 × 0 + 12 × 1 + 24 × 2 = 60 visit rows, but only 36 visitors.

</details>

**2. Change both the selection and precision.** Count people by the quarter of
their last visit. Would the resulting counts measure visits?

<details><summary>Solution 2</summary>


``` r
last_visit <- omop_anchor(visit, which = "last")
quarters <- omop_recipe(variables = list(last_quarter = omop_date(last_visit,
  omop_date_spec(precision = "quarter"))))
recipe_execute(quarters, out = "D_quarters", conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_quarters$last_quarter",
  useNA = "always", datasources = conns)$output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
```

```
#> D_quarters$last_quarter
#> 2020-Q3 2021-Q1 2023-Q4      NA
#>      12      12      12      12
```

There are 12 people in each of 2020-Q3, 2021-Q1 and 2023-Q4, and 12 with no visit.
Unlike the first-visit months above, these are the quarters of each person's last visit.
Each person contributes once; this table does not count all 60 visits.

</details>

## Recap

Choose an anchor for elapsed time and a precision for calendar summaries.
A person-level table selects or counts visits; a long table retains visit rows.
Always name which of those units your result counts.
